result.summary: Configure Guix to build non-GUI Bitcoin Core release binaries (bitcoind and CLI utilities) for x86_64 and aarch64 Linux as static position-independent executables (-static-pie) linked against glibc 2.44. Patch glibc to eliminate non-deterministic /gnu/store paths and disable runtime dlopen in NSS modules. Update symbol-check.py and security-check.py to validate static ELF binaries without dynamic linkers.
result.problem: Official Linux release binaries dynamically link against glibc, preventing them from running on non-glibc distributions like Alpine Linux and on distributions shipping older glibc versions. Dynamic linking also blocks certain security hardening features such as pointer authentication on aarch64 (#19075).
evidence: PR release notes state: 'Release binaries for x86_64 and aarch64 Linux (except for bitcoin-qt) are now compiled with -static-pie, making them more portable. They can now be run on non-glibc based systems, as well as on systems than ship with older glibcs, than were previously supported.'
Description notes testing across Alpine, Debian, CentOS, NixOS, and Ubuntu.
result.scope_notes: Touches Guix manifests, glibc patches, and binary check scripts. Disables dynamic NSS module lookups in glibc, meaning resolution for LDAP, SSSD, or mDNS (.local) domains will not work in static release binaries.
result.changed_since_previous: Now based on #36531, using Guix --load-path for local modules in contrib/guix/guix-build instead of setting GUIX_PACKAGE_PATH.
result.card: Configures Guix to build Linux x86_64 and aarch64 release binaries (excluding bitcoin-qt) as static position-independent executables (-static-pie) linked against glibc 2.44. This allows official Linux release binaries to run across distributions with older glibc versions or non-glibc libcs like Alpine, while resolving issue #19075 to permit aarch64 pointer authentication. A trade-off is that name resolution requiring dynamic NSS modules like LDAP or mDNS will no longer function in bitcoind. Symbol and security verification scripts are updated to assert properties of static ELF executables. This PR is based on #36531.

risk.why: Alters the libc linking model and patches glibc for official Linux release binaries, which could cause runtime crashes or DNS lookup failures on user machines.
